claims.text: Elliott Avenue West & West Harrison Street had 8 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are Elliott Avenue West & West Harrison Street's own: the city's record places 78 of the 88 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $548,000 a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.2 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $82,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.1 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $43,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 4th Avenue West, Elliott Avenue West, West Harrison Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
